1. DESIGN. The CTO's ruling @606e7d14ce ADOPTED the object-scoped read the packet declares and BARRED the publisher copy. The packet meets its four conditions: the registry vintage (blob 99b8eeb54f) and the ARN list are printed; the ban comment was amended in the same commit as the statement (@9f21dedfd8); the plans are 0 to destroy and every IAM key is additive; the bucket map is the one registry-derived value the directory root already sets. S94 stays the precondition (_authz/loaders.py:106-114 @4ceb7f8361); pitched to the CTO, carved out of the token.
2. WHY EARLIER PROOFS PASSED -- two independent reasons, the second found this pass. (i) The wrong IDENTITY: rtf-2 and rtf-8 arm (e) ran in-process under operator credentials. (ii) The wrong FILE LAYOUT (row S98): in the repository _ids/raw_keys.json sits beside _ids/ids.py, so an in-process import resolves ids.py:64 RAW_KEYS_PATH to a directory that HAS the file; every deployed zip flattens ids.py to the package root WITHOUT it (0 of 7). The identity bar is necessary and NOT sufficient: a served-path proof runs the DEPLOYED BYTES under the deployed role -- this pass's arm (f) did, which is why it failed while every configuration arm (e) passed.
3.
